packages.headline: ‘90s style sci-fi horror Derelikt launches Nov 13 on PS5

sources.label: PlayStation Blog
sources.evidenceText:
Solo dev Philipp Jensen reveals the secrets behind the title, which emulates PSOne-era aesthetic.
‘90s style sci-fi horror Derelikt launches Nov 13 on PS5
Back in 1999, gaming was good. Games that were released late in the original PlayStation generation squeezed the last drop of performance out of the hardware, resulting in impressive visuals and all-time classics whose sequels we still play today. Fast forward 26 years and we’re excited to announce that our sci-fi horror game Derelikt will make you feel like your console shed 5 generations when it launches on PlayStation 5 on November 13.
Derelikt takes place aboard Von Neumann Outpost, grafted onto an anomalous asteroid discovered in Saturn’s orbit. Things are rough. The work is hard, home is a million miles away, and people are stressed out. Plus, a mysterious drone is driving everyone closer to their breaking point…
You arrive as an outside contractor tasked with finding out the fate of Excavation Team Delta, who went missing on the derelict surface. What you discover turns things from bad to worse fast! The halls are dark, the systems are failing, and the survivors that you come across aren’t telling the same story. Nailing that feeling of not being able to trust those around you, while simultaneously coming face to face with truly out-of-this-world horrors, was paramount for us.
The Von Neumann Outpost is well stocked with an arsenal of traditional weapons, and as you progress, you might even find a few more outlandish weapon prototypes and even alien weapons at your disposal. There are also over a dozen to interact with in Derelikt, each featuring their own secrets, and agendas. Some are useful, some are dangerous, some are doomed, and some (let’s be real, most) are all three!
Derelikt is very much inspired by the PSOne-era of sci-fi horror, and it feels like a full-circle moment to be writing this today. The goal was to make it appear as if we found Derelikt on a CD-R in the dusty, long-abandoned storage unit of a defunct late-90s developer and simply ported it to modern platforms. I’m of the firm opinion that retro doesn’t have to mean crude and primitive, and I set out to create the most faithful homage to 5th generation graphics available on the market.
Our game features 100% lovingly hand-painted textures and vertex colour lighting. Affine Texture warping was deliberately implemented and mitigated in the next step by dynamically subdividing the geometry – just like the most high-end games of the era did – and the game also features retro-style full-motion CGI cutscenes. This way, a delicate balance was achieved – Derelikt looks aesthetically pleasing while still conceivably plausible on period hardware. Our team made a conscious effort to implement modern game design while keeping the core feeling and charm of that era of sci-fi horror intact, including an option for players to toggle on or off effects to match their particular taste.
Derelikt has been in development in some form since late 2021 and has had a turbulent and exciting development journey. We hope the game is as wild a ride for players as it has been to develop!

Nintendo declares November 1 "Pikmin Day" in recognition of all things Pikmin
This past weekend, Nintendo hosted a Pikmin Day Direct presentation. The showcase included the announcement of Nov. 1 as Pikmin Day, a new look at the enhanced features and gameplay of the upcoming Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy game coming exclusively to the Nintendo Switch 2 system Nov. 12, updates on the Pikmin Bloom smartphone app¹ and the reveal of an ongoing short movie series titled “Hello! Pikmin”.
Pikmin creator Shigeru Miyamoto kicked off the Pikmin Day Direct detailing the significance of the selected date for Pikmin Day. Nov. 1 was chosen as a tribute to the original three Red, Blue and Yellow Pikmin, with the date 11.1 resembling them standing in a line.
A new trailer for the Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy game was also shown. The showcase featured the new Dandori Academy, where players can improve their planning and treasure-collecting skills and test them in timed challenges and weekend exams to earn in-game medals. As announced during the presentation, a free demo of Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy featuring the Sun-Speckled Terrace opening area in the main story and two stages in Dandori Academy will be available later today on Nintendo eShop. Additionally, a new Nintendo Treehouse: Plays video showcasing some of the new additions including Dandori Academy gameplay is available to watch here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6x-yH4wkOYQ
An update is also coming to the Pikmin Bloom app this winter, including a new adventure in which users will explore caves, face off against creatures and collect in-game treasures. Also, users can test their Dandori skills by linking their app with Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy and taking on exams in the game to get special in-app rewards, including a cave map.
In the presentation, Mr. Miyamoto was joined by actress Fuka Koshiba, who is known for knitting a variety of Pikmin-inspired hats and sharing them on Instagram. Ms. Koshiba will help bring the fun and excitement of exploring the world of Pikmin to more people.
Fans can dive into the world of Pikmin on Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch with all four mainline Pikmin games available to play, from the first game through Pikmin 4 . There’s even more Pikmin charm to discover with the new Pikmin Ability Collection, which launched on Pikmin Day exclusively at Nintendo NEW YORK , Nintendo SAN FRANCISCO and the Nintendo Store . Inspired by the distinctive abilities of each Pikmin type, the collection brings their in-game strengths to playful products fans can enjoy every day.
Finally, two episodes of “Hello! Pikmin”, a new ongoing series of short movies produced by Nintendo Pictures, are available now on the Nintendo Today! app² and other Nintendo channels.

sources.label: PlayStation Blog

PlayStation Studios and third-party developers reflect on most-surprising games.
20 years of PlayStation Store – devs share the great games that surprised them most
For 20 years, PlayStation Store has connected players with games of all shapes and sizes, from blockbuster adventures to indie delights and everything in between.
To mark the occasion, we asked developers from PlayStation Studios and third-party studios to reflect on a great game from the past 20 years that caught them by surprise. Not necessarily their favorite game of all time, but one they didn’t expect to enjoy as much as they did, or that won them over in an unexpected way.
You can also check out the 20 Years of PlayStation Store Showcase when it goes live today (11:00am local time), where you can explore deals on games and a curated selection of hand-picked hits.
Now, here’s what the developers shared regarding games from the past 20 years that surprised them:
“ The game that comes to mind is Balatro. While it’s based on the simple, familiar rules of poker, I became completely hooked on the sense of satisfaction that comes from seeing your scores grow bigger and bigger through progression and different combinations.
It’s a truly compelling game that reminds me why games are so much fun to play in the first place.”

packages.headline: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered fighter guide

sources.label: PlayStation Blog
sources.evidenceText:
From grappling mutants to cyborg tanks, discover which kaiju is right for you.
Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered fighter guide
With its giant-sized fanbase, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered has plenty of players ready to get tooth, nail, and claw stuck into its PlayStation 5 release on November 3. Although it would be understandable that newcomers might feel a little intimidated choosing between 12 world crushing kaiju, each with their own stats, moveset, and special abilities. Never fear – we have the rundown on which colossus matches your playstyle to ensure you’re the true king of the monsters.
The face which sank a thousand ships. Godzilla is the iconic kaiju who all other kaiju want to be, beat, or be friends with. As the game’s default character, the giant lizard is balanced for newbies and veterans alike, with a high amount of starting health and decent all-round stats.
Godzilla also possesses a tail useful enough for a mighty wake-up strike when he’s downed, and some fairly swift claws, so many of his melee combos are effective for beginners. But don’t rely too much on his high-energy pulse – while it’s formidable, the slow charge leaves him open to counters. Similarly, ranged attackers can take advantage of his relatively sluggish projectiles, so close that distance or you’ll be heading back to Monster Island with your giant tail between your legs.
Ideal for: Players annoyed at their friend for picking Heisei Godzilla.
In terms of film history, Godzilla 2000 is a more modern incarnation of the legendary lizard, reflecting a new era for the new millennium. Although he’s arguably a slightly more vulnerable version of his Heisei predecessor.
As a result, while Godzilla 2000 is a bit faster than his kaiju shoto fighter twin, he’s not quite as strong. He’s still fairly well balanced and arguably easier to use than Heisei, so makes for a solid alternative. And his distinctive purple dorsal plates look pretty cool, too.
There’s a reason why this fearsome three-headed beast is seen as Godzilla’s archnemesis. Giant wings, gravity beams, and a desire to annihilate humanity, the threat of King Ghidorah should never be taken lightly.
Ideal for: Players who want to dive straight in.

packages.headline: Players’ Choice: Vote for October’s best new game

sources.label: PlayStation Blog
sources.evidenceText:
It's time to vote for the best gaming experience from last month.
Players’ Choice: Vote for October’s best new game
Last month was filled with an extensive release of games ranging from high octane racing to covert missions! Some big new releases included Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse, Phantom Blade Zero, Silver Pines, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve. Which game was your favorite? How does it work? At the end of every month, PlayStation Blog will open a poll where you can vote for the best new game released that month. After the polls close we will tally your votes, and announce the winner on our social channels and PlayStation.Blog.
What is the voting criteria? That’s up to you! If you were only able to recommend one new release to a friend that month, which would it be? Note: re-released games don’t qualify, but remakes do. We define remakes as ambitious, larger-scale rebuilds such as Resident Evil 4 (2023) and Final Fantasy VII Remake.
How are nominees decided? The PlayStation Blog editorial team will gather a list of that month’s most noteworthy releases and use it to seed the poll.

packages.headline: World of Warcraft: Forever – How Controller Support Reimagines the Way We Can Play in Azeroth

sources.label: Xbox Wire
sources.evidenceText:
My approach to World of Warcraft has largely been one of logging in and enjoying a casual adventure in Azeroth. I’m not messing around with macros or On November 4, players can return to a nostalgic world many grew up with – now with the freedom to play wherever and whenever they choose with Gamepad (Alpha) support.
World of Warcraft: Forever – How Controller Support Reimagines the Way We Can Play in Azeroth
With official Gamepad (Alpha) support available at launch, players can enjoy World of Warcraft from the palm of their hands.
My approach to World of Warcraft has largely been one of logging in and enjoying a casual adventure in Azeroth. I’m not messing around with macros or trying to carry a team through a dungeon. I’m more than happy to spend my time chewing on scenery and gobbling up lore. Yes, I’m that guy that wants to know exactly why he must fell 15 trolls.
This taps into one of the many things that makes World of Warcraft great, in that Blizzard wants to make sure there’s a WoW experience that suits everybody. Whether it’s through PC hardware support, innovations in battle mechanics like Single-Button Assistant, and rolling out numerous accessibility features such as Text to Speech, the game constantly hits it out of the park for creating a world for so many players to access and enjoy.
This is one of the things that has made me excited for World of Warcraft: Forever , in that Blizzard can now take all the years of learned knowledge of creating a welcoming Azeroth and return us to an age when it still felt fresh and unknown; like an adventure every time you logged in – and now we’ll be able to play with a controller in our hands thanks to Gamepad (Alpha) support.
I suppose I should back up just a bit to give you a refresher on what World of Warcraft: Forever is and why it’s a pretty big deal. Essentially, we’ll  return to a version of the game’s world that is very similar to the WoW that arrived in 2004, but with many new stories, locations, and improved features that work to strike that middle ground between that Classic feel, mixed with added improvements to make the experience welcoming for newcomers. And it’s going to stay that way, hence the Forever in the game’s title.
Think of Forever as filling the gaps of Azeroth with denser content to keep the Classic vibes in play. And it’s all included in your current subscription, so there’s no additional purchase required to experience this old-new world. And one of those new ways to experience Azeroth will influence not only how to play but also where.
My personal PC gaming rig is about the size of a game console, which occasionally finds a home next to my XBOX Series X|S in the living room; I’m rocking an AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D and ASUS Prime Radeon RX 9070 all in a small form factor Fractal Ridge case. Now with World of Warcraft: Forever and its Gamepad (Alpha) support, I’m as close as I’ve ever been to a console-like Warcraft experience – and it’s awesome.

VRChat社は10月29日、同社が提供するソーシャルプラットフォーム『VRChat』についてのアンケート結果を受けた方針を提示。そのなかで、「AI生成」というラベルや、AI生成コンテンツを除外する検索フィルターを追加する予定はないことを明らかにした。この決定に対してユーザーからの反発が相次いでおり、Steamでは低評価レビューやストアページに「人工知能」タグをつけるといった行動が確認できる。
『VRChat』は、ワールドと呼ばれる仮想空間にて、世界中のユーザー同士が自身のアバターを通じて交流できるソーシャルプラットフォームだ。Steam/Viveport/Meta Quest/Pico/iOS/Android向けに基本プレイ無料にて提供されており、VRデバイスがなくても利用できる「デスクトップモード」も存在する。
こうした事態を受けて、VRChat社は10月7日に声明を発表。クリエイターガイドラインを更新し、実際のワールドの内容と異なるサムネイル画像を使用することを禁止。また、説明文についても誤解を招く表現を使わないようにと案内した。あわせて「VRChatとAI：あなたの線引きは？」と題したユーザーアンケートを実施していた（ 関連記事 ）。
A few weeks ago, we asked the community to submit feedback on how they felt about AI in VRChat. Here's our takeaways and next steps: https://t.co/egpByRfeRD
こうした結果を踏まえて、VRChat社は人間が制作したことを明示する「Human-authored」ラベルや、使用ツールの項目の追加は検討しているものの、AI生成を明示するラベルやフィルターを追加する予定はないとのことだ。こうした機能を追加することで、AIを利用したワールドを手作業のように見せかけるクリエイターの登場や、AIを使用していないにも関わらず嫌がらせを受けるような事態を懸念しており、AI利用の有無を詮索する“探偵行為”が発生することは、望まない負の連鎖を生み出す恐れがあるとしている。
VRChat now has "AI" tag on steam pic.twitter.com/eYUvwcNNTl
本作では、クリエイターが作成したさまざまなワールドを訪れることが楽しみの一つとなっている。一方で昨今は生成AIによるワールドの粗製乱造や、ワールドのサムネイルがAIによって生成されているが、ワールドの実態と一致しない、いわゆるサムネイル詐欺が増加していることにユーザーが不満を覚えている状況であった。

packages.headline: Terminally Ill GTA 6 Fan Dies 3 Weeks Before Game's Launch, Fans Pay Their Respects

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
A terminally ill GTA 6 fan has died three weeks before the game's launch.
Terminally Ill GTA 6 Fan Dies 3 Weeks Before Game's Launch, Fans Pay Their Respects
Back in August, a man named Jerry, known online as Void Only, made a viral TikTok video revealing that he had been hospitalized due to an interstitial lung disease and was in need of a lung transplant. However, he noted that his unique situation meant that his lungs were attached to his chest wall, and any surgery would be bloody and dangerous. In that same post, he noted that he just wanted to play GTA 6, and poked fun at Rockstar's many delays for the game. In the comments, fellow players rallied around him and were rooting for him to keep going until the release of GTA 6.
A GoFundMe was set up to pay for his transplant and other needs, with supporters donating $50,000 in a matter of days . In September, Jerry got his transplant, but various complications eventually caused him to lose function of his body. Jerry's sister confirmed via his socials that he died over the weekend, but was extremely appreciative of all of the people who tried to help and support him. The news comes just three weeks before GTA 6's release, which Jerry had planned to stream with his community once it was released.
In the comments of his sister's post, fans expressed sadness over Jerry not being able to make it to the release of the game he'd been excitedly waiting so long to play.
"I'm adding Void to my gamertag in his honor when GTA releases," said another.
This tragic outcome has left supporters devastated. Jerry himself stayed optimistic in his final months and kept a positive attitude, prompting fans to echo his enthusiasm. Jerry's sister also noted that his mother is planning to do a balloon release in his honor, and more details will be shared at a later date.

『Rain98』は、1998年の東京で少女とともに世界滅亡の儀式を進める、サイコサスペンス&ロマンスADVである。本作の舞台は1998年の東京。メインキャラクターの雨原玲奈は、どこか物憂げな謎めいた少女だ。本作でプレイヤーは、不穏で危うい雨原玲奈と共に世界滅亡の儀式をおこなう。20世紀末の東京を巡りながら、二人だけの儀式を進めていき、その過程では彼女の秘密にも近づいていくのだという。孤独な若者たちの選択が、世界の運命を決めるのだという。なお雨原玲奈のCVは声優の土屋李央さんが担当する。

一方で、2027年初頭には、体験版に向け、シナリオ追加を含めた大型アップデートを実施する予定とのこと。プレイヤーからのフィードバックを参考にしつつ、『Rain98』の進捗を伝えていくという。そして正式な発売日については、より確かな見通しが立ったタイミングでの発表となるようで、続報に期待したいところだ。

REMIMORY has delayed the Early Access version of “anime-style survival adventure” Castaway Diary: Portal to the Unknown Isles from its previously planned 2026 release window to 2027, as well as announced a four-step roadmap leading up to the Early Access launch. It will be available for PC via Steam . “We sincerely apologize for having to announce a delay to everyone eagerly waiting for the game,” said the REMIMORY development team in a press release. “However, to repay the tremendous support you have shown us, we promise to return with an experience truly worth the wait. We will continue active development while communicating closely with players through our Steam Community Hub, so please keep cheering us on.”
Here are the latest details, via REMIMORY:
Castaway Diary: Portal to the Unknown Isles is a bright, casual survival sandbox game following the adventures of girls stranded on an uncharted island. Setting itself apart from conventional grim and tension-heavy survival games, it is designed to offer a relaxed and leisurely island survival life alongside charming anime-style characters—featuring gathering, fishing, and cooking, as well as highly customizable housing, farming, and character customization through crafted outfits. Players can also explore uncharted islands and dungeons on mounts, defeat monsters, and team up in up to four-player online cooperative multiplayer to pioneer the island and conquer dungeons together.

Dark visual novel PRIMA MATERIA announced for PC
Publisher Top Hat Studios and Synergia developer Radi Art have announced PRIMA MATERIA , a dark visual novel coming to PC via Steam in 2027.
PRIMA MATERIA is a dark surreal visual novel set in a sterilized wasteland ruled by Angels, where consciousness is harvested, brewed, and sold. Mana , a Mind Digger who survives by eating minds, takes one last job: fixing a demi-angel worth keeping whole.
In the Concrete Sea, an endless grey wasteland beneath a sun that never sets, consciousness is a resource. Angels farm humans for it, brewing it over centuries into Prima Materia, a luminous orange liquid that can be distilled and most importantly, consumed. Mana is a Mind Digger, someone who carves psyches for a living, extracting and eating what others don’t want to carry anymore: guilt, fear, memories.
Her self-contained existence collapses with the arrival of Girin: the rebellious daughter of an ancient Angel, dropped at Mana’s door with a simple request to “fix” her, in exchange for an infinite supply of Prima Materia. Girin’s untamable nature doesn’t make things easy, but it’s what lies deep inside her mind that scares Mana. Something old and protective is waiting, something that recognizes Mana for what she is and that has no interest in letting her anywhere near Girin’s core.
Here is an overview of the game, via Top Hat Studios:
“I must reject morality because it serves those in power; this is a mechanical world where I am nothing but a mechanical device and so is everyone else. Everything’s real, nothing’s in your head.”

Nintendo announces Zelda: Ocarina of Time UK midnight launch, with free N64 boxes up for grabs
Nintendo is hosting a UK midnight launch for Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s Switch 2 remake
Nintendo is holding an official UK midnight launch event for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s Switch 2 remake, with attendees receiving special N64 box replicas.
The midnight launch event for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time will take place at the Nintendo store at Argos Tottenham Court Road, London, this Wednesday evening, ahead of the game’s release on Thursday, November 5.
Those who buy the game at the midnight launch event will receive a free Nintendo 64 box replica, based on the game’s UK box design, complete with an inner tray and slipcase designed to fit the Nintendo Switch 2 game. Purchasers will also receive an Ocarina key ring, while supplies last.
The ‘Nintendo Experience Zone’ has been operating within Tottenham Court Road’s Argos store since earlier this year and is stocked with consoles, games, and merchandise for Nintendo games like Zelda, Mario, and Animal Crossing.
When it was announced, the Argos pop-up was said to be temporary. It follows last year’s Nintendo London pop-up store, which was open in Westfield Shopping Centre for around a month last October, selling merchandise previously only available at Nintendo‘s permanent stores in Tokyo, Osaka, Kyoto, San Francisco, and New York.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is set to release on November 5 for Nintendo Switch 2. A limited edition 40th Anniversary Switch 2 console and Pro Controller was released ahead of the game last week.

packages.headline: Xbox COO who left after just 3 months shoots down claims she was 'fired for a policy violation,' says her story is about 'core values'

sources.label: PC Gamer
sources.evidenceText:
Helen Chiang, who became the Xbox division's first chief operating officer in July, says she has "serious concerns" about how her case was handled.
Xbox COO who left after just 3 months shoots down claims she was 'fired for a policy violation,' says her story is about 'core values'
"This is not how I ever imagined my story here would end. And it is not the whole story."
Longtime Microsoft executive Helen Chiang was made Xbox's first-ever chief operating officer as part of the 'reset' in July, a role that gave her "end-to-end P&L responsibility across content, hardware, platform, and services." Then, just three months later and with virtually no fanfare, she was gone , amidst an anonymous claim that she was "terminated for policy violations."
The record-straightening did not get into why Chiang did leave Xbox, although she seemed to imply that it was not an amicable departure: "I believe in fairness, accountability, and holding ourselves to the standards we expect of others. Those standards only mean something when they're applied consistently. I have serious concerns about how they were applied in my case, and I believe those concerns deserve to be taken seriously."
The sudden split seemed doubly strange because prior to taking the COO job at Xbox, Chiang spent more than 20 years at Microsoft, nearly all of it with the Xbox division—rising from Xbox platform business manager in 2007 to corporate vice president of the Minecraft franchise in 2020, a position she held for more than six years. The memo announcing Chiang's departure was also notably restrained: "Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft today," Xbox CEO Asha Sharma wrote. "I'm grateful for her years of service and wish her well."
